Payment reminder email for HVAC companies

HVAC billing mixes small repair tickets, big installs, card memberships and commercial net 30 accounts. Here is a reminder schedule and wording that fits each.

Checked 2026-11-21. Menus in other products change, so a label may differ slightly on your screen.

Short answer: for an HVAC company, send a friendly reminder on or just before the due date, an overdue note about a week later, a firmer one at about two weeks, and a final notice near 30 days. Each one names the job, the invoice number and the amount, attaches the invoice, and says how to pay. Memberships, installs and commercial accounts each need slightly different timing, covered below.

For the general method, see how to chase overdue invoices by email. This page covers what is specific to HVAC.

Sort invoices by type before you chase

  • Service calls and repairs. Usually due on completion or in a few days. The diagnostic fee can be the line people question, so name it on the reminder.
  • Installs. A deposit up front and a balance on completion. Late balances are large, so they get a personal touch early.
  • Financed installs. The customer owes the finance company, not you. Programs generally pay the contractor after the customer signs off that the work is complete, so a "late" payment is often a missing completion form, not a customer problem. Check your program's own terms.
  • Memberships and maintenance agreements. Monthly or yearly, usually on a card. The usual problem is a declined or expired card, not refusal.
  • Commercial accounts. Often net 30 and paid by an accounts payable clerk who needs a purchase order number.

A reminder schedule that fits HVAC billing

  1. Service calls: a friendly note on the due date, an overdue note at 7 days, a firmer one at 14, a final notice at 30.
  2. Install balances: a friendly note 2 days before the due date, then a phone call at 3 days late instead of a second email. Follow with the firmer and final emails at 14 and 30 days.
  3. Financed installs: first check whether the finance company has your completion paperwork. Chase the customer only if the paperwork is in and the customer owes a deposit or a part the loan does not cover.
  4. Memberships: email the day a card is declined, not a week later. Offer a pay link to update the card. Follow up at 3 and 7 days, which is our suggestion rather than a rule.
  5. Commercial net 30: a note a few days before the due date asking whether they have what they need, such as a PO number. Then 7, 14 and 30 days late.

For how many reminders is too many, see how often to send invoice reminders.

Check before you send

  • Payment already taken. The tech may have run the card on the tablet, and it has not synced to your books yet. Look at the job record first.
  • An open callback or warranty visit. If the same equipment is still being looked at, hold the reminder until that visit is done. Chasing payment for a unit that is not working again goes badly.
  • Finance paperwork not submitted. If the job is financed, find out whether your completion form went in. The money may be waiting on you.
  • A plan that covers the visit. A membership customer may owe nothing, or only a discounted amount, for this visit. Check the plan before you send a full-price reminder.

Busy season: when billing falls behind

In the first hot week or cold snap, techs work late and invoices go out days after the job. A customer cannot be late on an invoice they have not received. Before you chase anyone in a rush, check that the invoice was actually sent and that the due date counts from the day it went out. Chasing a customer for a bill they never saw costs you the goodwill that makes a membership renew.

Wording you can copy

1. Friendly reminder, repair or service call

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] - [job description], due [due date] Hi [name], Thanks for having us out on [service date]. This is a friendly reminder that invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is due on [due date]. A copy is attached, including the diagnostic fee and repair details. You can pay here: [pay link] If you have a question about any line, reply and I will go through it with you. [your name] [company name]

2. Overdue, membership card declined

Subject: Your [company name] maintenance plan payment did not go through Hi [name], Your payment of [amount] for your [plan name] maintenance plan did not go through on [date]. This is usually an expired or replaced card. You can update your card here: [pay link] Your plan stays active while we sort this out, and your next tune-up is still booked for [visit date]. If you would rather pay another way, just reply. [your name] [company name]

3. Firmer, install balance or commercial invoice

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] is now [days] days overdue Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount], for [job description / PO number], was due on [due date] and we have not received payment. A copy is attached. Could you let me know when we can expect it? If you need a different document, a W-9, or a PO number added, tell me and I will send it today. You can pay here: [pay link] [your name] [company name], [phone]

4. Final notice

Subject: Final notice: invoice [invoice number] Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is now [days] days overdue, and I have not had a reply to my earlier notes. Please pay by [date]. If we have not heard from you by then, we will [pause scheduled maintenance visits / apply the late fee in our agreement]. If something has gone wrong, call me on [phone] and we can set up a payment plan. [your name] [company name]

Only state a consequence you are entitled to and will carry out. Late fees and their amounts depend on your signed agreement and state law. If you mention a lien on a job, rules on liens vary by state, so check yours first. This is not legal advice.

A short text version

Many customers read a text faster than an email, especially on a service call day. Only text customers who have agreed to get texts from you, for example on the work order, and stop if they reply STOP. Texting rules are federal and some states add their own.

Hi [name], it's [company name]. Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] from your [service date] visit is still open. Pay here: [pay link]. Questions? Reply or call [phone]. Reply STOP to opt out.

What the built-in tools cannot do

QuickBooks Online and most field service software can send the same reminder to everyone. They generally cannot tell a declined membership card from a late commercial invoice, or let you read each automatic message first. Standard QuickBooks Online reminders cannot leave one customer out. QuickBooks Online Advanced can, using workflows, and one Intuit community answer describes how; check it in your own account. See how to stop QuickBooks invoice reminders for one customer. Telling these cases apart is the part that takes your time in the busy months.
